blocks.heading: Improving productivity
blocks.text: Productivity can improve through relevant skills, suitable technology, better layout, maintenance, reliable inputs, motivation and effective coordination. Trace the mechanism: less time waiting for materials can increase acceptable output per hour; fewer defects can increase usable output from the same input. Training can be on-the-job or off-the-job according to need and available expertise. An improvement requires actual use and suitable conditions, not simply buying a machine or announcing a target. Extra output achieved solely by proportionately extra hours is not a productivity gain.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Nera Assembly loses time walking between distant storage and workstations. A practical layout change can reduce handling time and increase acceptable units per labour hour without asking for longer shifts. Check safety and quality so the faster process does not merely create defects.
